**Allowed origins** are set in the `origin` callback of the `cors({...})` middleware in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`. The callback starts at line 21. It echoes the request's origin back if it matches one of these:

- `http://localhost:4200`, as an exact match (line 24).
- Any origin ending in `.pages.dev` (line 25).
- Any origin ending in `.workers.dev` (line 26).

A request with no `Origin` header gets `null`, and so does any other origin. The same `cors` block also sets these values:

- `allowMethods`: `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`.
- `allowHeaders`: `Content-Type`, `Authorization`.
- `maxAge`: `86400`.

**Adding a custom domain:** add another condition inside the `if (...)` at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`, using `||`.

- For one exact origin, add `origin === 'https://app.example.com'`.
- For a domain and its subdomains, use a check like `origin.endsWith('.example.com')`.
- Don't add it to an array. Hono treats array entries as literal strings, so wildcards won't match. This is why the code uses a function.

For a bare-domain suffix match, prefer an exact origin or a `.`-prefixed `endsWith`. A check like `endsWith('example.com')` would also match `evilexample.com`.

The docs also say to update `frontend/src/environments/environment.prod.ts` if the Worker URL changes. They cover CORS in `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4 and `docs/code/worker/src/index.md`.
